title: Exact Context Manifest identity contract (G0 freeze)

identity.projectId: Required. The project-scoped canonical project id; a Manifest can never be replayed or confirmed across projects.
identity.projectStateRevision: Required. The single revision from which the projection was read; part of the Manifest's four-layer identity.
identity.contextPolicyVersion: Required. The deterministic context-projection policy version that selected the fields.
identity.contextProjectionSchemaVersion: Required. The schema version of the projection input/output shapes.
identity.contextProjectionHash: Required. SHA-256 of the canonicalized projection bytes; proves what was selected, not that conclusions are correct.
identity.exactRequestHash: Required for any outbound-capable Manifest. SHA-256 of the serialized exact request body bytes actually sent; distinct from the projection hash.
identity.exactRequestBody: Required for any outbound-capable Manifest. Stored locally and protected; never logged, never in backups summaries, absent for a no-provider snapshot.
identity.exactRequestBytes: Required. Byte length of the exact request body; used for size caps and comparisons.
identity.providerIdentity: Required when a Provider attempt exists: providerId, family, model, baseUrlOrigin, locality, config generation.
identity.providerGeneration: Required when a Provider attempt exists; any generation change makes the Manifest stale.
identity.manifestId: System-generated, stable; rebuilds produce a new manifestId and version while the old one stays history.
identity.reviewId: The owning Review; one Review may hold a history of Manifests, only the current one is sendable.

objectSelection: active Brief fields selected by the projection policy
explicitly selected Evidence references and summaries
explicitly selected Memory items (item ids, versions, hashes)
relevant prior Review outcome summary (deterministic projection only)
ordering: deterministic canonical order: fixed category order as listed in objectSelection
within each category, objects ordered by ascending object id
object fields serialized in canonical key order
array items keep their semantic order and are never sorted silently when order carries meaning
the same inputs, policy version, and schema version always produce byte-identical projection input
canonicalization: Canonical JSON serialization: object keys sorted lexicographically by UTF-16 code unit, no insignificant whitespace, no trailing newline inside the hashed byte sequence, Unicode normalized to NFC for user text before hashing. The canonicalization is a code-signed, versioned policy resource; research text can never modify it.
hashAlgorithm: SHA-256 over the canonicalized bytes, rendered as lowercase hex (64 characters). contextProjectionHash and exactRequestHash use this algorithm.
encoding: UTF-8 for all serialized projection and request bytes; byte length (exactRequestBytes) is measured over the UTF-8 byte sequence.
excludedMutableFields: UI theme, language, and viewport preferences
search query text and result cursor
providerMetadataBoundary: The Manifest stores Provider identity snapshot and generation only. Secrets, Authorization headers, hidden reasoning, and raw provider outputs are excluded from the Manifest and from every Receipt projection; the exactRequestBody is stored locally and protected, never transmitted as metadata.
previewPayloadConsistency: The user-visible preview and the real payload are produced from the same projection input and the same serializer. Equality is defined by exactRequestHash: the preview must display the exact body whose hash will be sent, and the send path must re-verify that the prepared body still hashes to the same exactRequestHash.
replayComparison: Immediately before any network I/O the Kernel re-opens a fresh single-read snapshot, recomputes the projection and request body, and compares projectStateRevision, contextProjectionHash, exactRequestHash, and Provider generation against the Manifest. Any mismatch transitions the Manifest to stale with a precise stale reason and performs zero network I/O. A changed revision with an unchanged payload still requires fresh user confirmation and never auto-sends.
snapshotRule: Projection reads and send-time revalidation each run inside one SQLite read snapshot; mixed-version reads across repositories are forbidden and fail closed.
